blocks.orig: This article will focus first and foremost on everything you need to know about what to wear (and bring) on your Tanzania safari. Before we have a look at actual pieces of clothing, let’s talk about the weather – the perfect conversation starter.
blocks.html: Above all, this article covers everything worth knowing about what to wear (and pack) for your Tanzania safari. Before we get to the clothes themselves, we will start with the weather – the ideal way to open any conversation.

blocks.orig: The dry season, which lasts from late June to early October, is when you may see the most wildlife in Tanzania. In the Serengeti, late January to early February offers the best chances to witness the wildebeest calving and the migration, respectively. The “long rains”, also known as the major rainy season in Tanzania, extend roughly from March to May.
blocks.html: You are likely to see the most wildlife in Tanzania during the dry season, which runs from late June until early October. In the Serengeti, your best chance of seeing the wildebeest calving and the migration comes from late January to early February respectively. The main rainy season in Tanzania, called the “long rains”, lasts more or less from March to May.

blocks.orig: It is advised to wear loose, comfortable, and easy-to-wash clothing. The idea is to bring only what you need because most camps and lodges will wash your clothes for a modest cost. There is no need to dress up for safaris because they are casual – and even with your practical safari clothes, you’ll cut an Instagram-worthy figure!
blocks.html: Our advice is to wear clothes that are loose, comfortable and simple to wash. Pack only the things you really need, as most lodges and camps will do your laundry for a small fee. Safaris are relaxed affairs, so dressing up is unnecessary – and you will still look Instagram-worthy in your practical safari outfit!

blocks.orig: Plan to wear layers so you can acclimatize to weather variations because, depending on the time of year, early morning game drives can be rather chilly while daytime temperatures can get quite warm. Instead of dark blue or black, which tends to draw tsetse flies, wear neutral or khaki-colored clothing so that you blind right in. Sunglasses, insect repellant, sunscreen, and wide-brimmed hats are essential. It’s recommended that you wear long pants, long-sleeved shirts, socks, and insect repellant to prevent mosquito bites after dusk. Here is a checklist of every piece of clothing you should take and what to wear on your Tanzania safari. So you can refer to it while you pack for your trip.
blocks.html: Bring layers so you can adjust to changes in the weather: at certain times of year the early morning game drives can feel quite cold, while it can become fairly hot during the day. Choose neutral or khaki-coloured clothes so you blend right in, rather than black or dark blue, which tend to attract tsetse flies. Wide-brimmed hats, sunscreen, insect repellent and sunglasses are a must. After dusk, we suggest long trousers, long-sleeved shirts, socks and insect repellent to protect you from mosquito bites. Below you will find a checklist of all the clothing to pack and what to wear on your Tanzania safari, so you can check it as you get your bags ready.

blocks.html: Light long trousers or zip-off trousers that convert to shorts

blocks.orig: Heavy sweater, gloves, and toque if traveling in the cold season
blocks.html: A thick jumper, gloves and a beanie if you travel during the cold season

blocks.html: A swimsuit – for the pool at your accommodation or for the Indian Ocean

blocks.orig: If you decide to explore Stone Town or any other part of Zanzibar other than the beach resorts before your safari, it’s best to dress modestly. Women shouldn’t dress in short skirts, thigh-high shorts, sleeveless shirts, or exposing shirts. However, Capri trousers or at least knee-length shorts, and of course long dresses and skirts are fine. For men, knee-length shorts or pants are appropriate.
blocks.html: Should you choose to visit Stone Town or anywhere else on Zanzibar outside the beach resorts before your safari, modest clothing is the best choice. Women should avoid short skirts, very short shorts, sleeveless tops or revealing shirts. Capri trousers or shorts that reach at least the knee are fine, as are long skirts and dresses, of course. Men can wear trousers or shorts that come down to the knee.
